locator: I q.14 a.1 co.: immaterialitas alicuius rei est ratio quod sit cognoscitiva
interpretation: Immateriality is the reason why a thing is cognitive, and the mode of knowledge follows the mode of immateriality: plants do not know because of their materiality, sense knows because it receives species without matter, intellect knows more because it is more separate from matter; God, in the highest degree of immateriality, is in the highest degree of knowledge. Read as: what is altogether immaterial, neither a matter-form composite nor a component of anything, has intellect. Not being a matter-form composite alone is not enough: a brute soul is no such composite but is a component of the animal and does not understand (I q.75 a.3, a.5; Codex P1 on #201). Interpretive step: the highest grade of immateriality is taken as intellectual.
